tasks.short: Answer site managers' and department heads' questions on budget rules, cost codes, approvals and spending control.

today.trigger: A Teams message or mail from a site manager, HR or operations lead asking how to book, budget or approve something.
steps: Read the question and find the relevant policy on SharePoint
Check the cost centre or budget position in AFAS or Power BI
Write an answer or call the person
Sometimes update the policy or a FAQ after repeated questions
drudgery: Answering the same questions about cost codes and approval limits each month
Looking up budget remaining for a cost centre by hand
today.time_sinks: Repeated questions from three sites, and pulling budget-versus-actual for one cost centre on request.

lenses.faster: A finance assistant in Teams answers policy and cost-code questions from the SharePoint policies and shows live budget-versus-actual, so the controller only handles the questions it cannot answer.
lenses.autonomous: Budget holders get a monthly message per cost centre with spend, remaining budget and items that break policy, without asking.
lenses.ambitious: Every budget holder at Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo gets proper coaching on their numbers, including flex worker spend from agency invoices, instead of only the loudest managers.
lenses.joy: No more repeat questions on which cost code a forklift repair goes to; the controller spends the time on the real conversations about overspend.
lenses.options: For a manager facing an overrun, the assistant drafts three options (shift budget, defer spend, accept overrun with a reason) with the effect on the site forecast.
lenses.altitude: The controller owns the policy content and the assistant's answer base, reviews the questions it got wrong and fixes the source documents.
reach: FP&A Analyst: routine budget-versus-actual explanations to budget holders
Bookkeeper: answering coding questions from requisitioners

tasks.human_edge: Judging when a request is really a control problem or a political issue between sites, and saying no to a manager in a way that keeps the relationship.
tasks.pattern_why: Questions are unstructured and the answer often needs judgement on exceptions; an assistant grounded in policies and data drafts, the controller stays accountable for advice.

in_practice.trigger: A budget holder asks a question in a Finance Teams channel, or the monthly budget close completes.
steps: Assistant retrieves the relevant SharePoint policy section and the cost centre's AFAS figures
Drafts an answer with the source cited
Answers standard questions directly; flags exceptions and approval questions to the controller
Controller reviews flagged items and updates the policy FAQ
in_practice.human_gate: Any answer that grants an exception, changes an approval limit or reallocates budget goes through the controller.
data_needed: Finance policies and approval matrix on SharePoint
Chart of accounts and cost centre list
Budget and actuals per cost centre
in_practice.logs_to: Teams channel history plus a question log in SharePoint used to improve the FAQ

evidence.claim: Microsoft 365 Copilot can answer questions grounded in SharePoint documents.
Routine policy questions make up most of the inbound volume to a controller.

risks: Assistant gives a confident wrong answer on an approval limit
Outdated policies on SharePoint get repeated as truth
Managers bypass the controller on issues that need a conversation
research_questions: How many budget and policy questions does the controller get per month, and what share repeat?
Are the SharePoint finance policies current enough to ground answers?
Do budget holders read a monthly cost centre message, or ignore it?

tasks.short: Dig into margins, costs per site and customer, and trends to find where we lose money or can improve.

today.trigger: Month close, a management question, or a cost line that looks off in Power BI.
steps: Export ledger and cost centre data from AFAS into Excel
Add volumes from operations and flex hours from agency portals
Build pivots per site, customer and cost type
Write findings and suggestions for the Finance Director and MT
drudgery: Combining exports from AFAS and three agency portals
Rebuilding the same pivots each month
today.time_sinks: Data preparation and reconciling flex hours to agency invoices take most of the time; analysis gets what is left.

lenses.faster: A standing data model joins AFAS ledger, agency hours and volumes, so the controller asks questions in plain language over it instead of building pivots.
lenses.autonomous: After each nightly refresh, variance checks flag cost lines per site or customer that move beyond a threshold, with a first explanation.
lenses.ambitious: Cost-to-serve per customer and per warehouse activity, done properly for the first time, so pricing and contract renewals are based on real margin.
lenses.joy: The controller stops copy-pasting exports and spends the time on why Venlo's cost per pallet rose.
lenses.options: For each finding, AI drafts several improvement scenarios (renegotiate agency rate, shift flex to fixed staff, reprice customer) with the euro effect.
lenses.altitude: The controller designs the margin model and the variance rules, and checks the explanations the system produces.
reach: Finance Director: first draft of MT finance pack

tasks.human_edge: Knowing the business behind the numbers: which customer is strategic, what happened on the floor in Tilburg, and which improvement operations will actually accept.
tasks.pattern_why: Data joining is deterministic, but choosing what matters and what to propose needs judgement; AI speeds analysis and drafting while the controller leads.

in_practice.trigger: Nightly AFAS extract refresh and month-end close.
steps: Deterministic pipeline joins AFAS ledger, agency hours and volumes into the Power BI model
Variance rules flag lines over threshold per site and customer
LLM drafts explanations and candidate actions per flag
Controller reviews, investigates the top items and writes the MT note
in_practice.human_gate: Controller decides which findings go to the Finance Director and MT.
data_needed: Operational volumes per site and customer
in_practice.logs_to: Power BI variance report and a findings log in SharePoint

evidence.claim: Copilot in Power BI can generate narrative summaries of report data.
Automated variance flags with drafted commentary cut analysis prep time substantially.

risks: Agency data quality makes cost-to-serve misleading
LLM explanations sound plausible but are wrong
Volume data from operations is not available in a clean form
research_questions: Can operational volumes per site and customer be extracted reliably each night?
Do agency portals offer exports or APIs for hours and rates?
Which past findings led to actual savings, and would the new set-up have found them sooner?

tasks.short: Prepare for and coordinate the year-end audit and internal checks on accounts and transactions.

today.trigger: Year-end audit planning by the external auditor, or an internal control review.
steps: Receive the auditor's request list (PBC list)
Gather reconciliations, contracts, invoices and payroll evidence from AFAS and SharePoint
Assign items to accountants and bookkeepers and chase them
Answer auditor questions and agree adjustments
drudgery: Pulling samples of invoices and payment proofs one by one
Tracking the PBC list in Excel
today.time_sinks: Collecting and matching evidence for samples, and the back-and-forth with the auditor on open items.

lenses.faster: An agent pulls sample evidence (invoice, PO, payment from the Rabobank statement) from AFAS and SharePoint and assembles it per PBC item, so the controller only reviews.
lenses.autonomous: Continuous checks run monthly: duplicate payments, vendor bank account changes, journal entries posted by unusual users or outside hours, payroll to AFAS headcount.
lenses.ambitious: Full-population testing of payments and journals instead of samples, so audit adjustments drop and the auditor relies more on internal controls.
lenses.joy: No more digging through folders for a 2025 invoice; the controller focuses on the judgement items the auditor raises.
lenses.options: For each audit finding, AI drafts alternative remediation plans with effort and risk reduction.
lenses.altitude: The controller designs the control-testing rules and the evidence library, and reviews exceptions rather than gathering.
reach: Accountant: preparing balance sheet reconciliations for audit
Bookkeeper: answering sample requests on AP and AR

tasks.human_edge: Negotiating with the auditor on judgement items, deciding which adjustments to accept, and signing off as the responsible person.
tasks.pattern_why: Several steps across systems with exceptions; evidence packs and test results must be reviewed by the controller before they go to the auditor.

in_practice.trigger: Auditor uploads a PBC list or sample selection; monthly control tests on the closing calendar.
steps: Agent parses the PBC list and sample selection
Retrieves documents and ledger lines from AFAS, SharePoint and bank statements
Builds evidence folders and marks missing items with an owner
Runs rule-based tests over the full population and lists exceptions
Controller reviews and releases to the auditor
in_practice.human_gate: Controller approves every evidence pack and every exception explanation before sharing with the auditor.
in_practice.logs_to: PBC tracker on SharePoint with status and reviewer per item

evidence.claim: Rule-based full-population tests on journals and payments are established audit analytics practice.
An LLM agent can assemble evidence packs from document stores against a request list.

risks: Wrong document attached to a sample undermines auditor trust
Payroll evidence contains personal data, so AVG/GDPR access limits apply
Auditor may not accept AI-assembled evidence without a clear trail
research_questions: Will the external auditor accept evidence packs and full-population tests prepared this way?
What share of PBC items can be retrieved from AFAS and SharePoint without manual search?
How many hours did the last audit take internally, by item type?

tasks.short: Write and update internal control rules: approval limits, cash and credit procedures, closing procedures.

today.trigger: Audit management letter, a new process (e.g. new agency contract), an incident, or the annual policy review.
steps: Review the existing procedure and the issue raised
Draft new rules in Word, including approval matrix
Discuss with Finance Director and process owners
Publish on SharePoint and configure where possible in AFAS workflows
drudgery: Formatting and keeping procedures consistent with each other
Translating the approval matrix into AFAS workflow settings by hand
today.time_sinks: Writing from scratch and aligning wording across many related procedures.

lenses.faster: AI drafts a procedure from the issue, the current text and good-practice controls, and checks it for conflicts with other procedures; the controller edits.
lenses.autonomous: When an audit letter or incident is logged, a draft update to the affected procedure is prepared and queued for review.
lenses.ambitious: A complete, consistent control framework covering procure to pay, order to cash, payroll and flex workers, with each control mapped to its test and owner.
lenses.joy: The controller no longer stares at a blank page; they decide on risk appetite and the trade-off with workload.
lenses.options: Draft three variants of a control (strict, balanced, light) with the risk they cover and the workload they add.
lenses.altitude: The controller maintains the control framework and its mapping to AFAS settings and tests, not the individual documents.
reach: Finance Director: drafting the finance governance section
Credit and Collections Officer: credit limit procedure drafts

tasks.human_edge: Choosing the right risk level for this company, getting buy-in from site managers, and owning the controls in front of the auditor.
tasks.pattern_why: Drafting is mostly generated text, but the decisions about risk and fit are the controller's; output must be approved before it applies.

in_practice.trigger: New audit finding, incident, process change, or annual review date.
steps: Collect current procedure, related procedures and the trigger issue
LLM drafts updated procedure and approval matrix in house style
LLM checks conflicts with other procedures and lists AFAS settings to change
Controller edits, Finance Director approves, published on SharePoint
in_practice.human_gate: Finance Director approves every procedure change before publication.
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint version history and a control register in Excel

evidence.claim: Copilot in Word drafts and rewrites documents from existing files.
LLMs can check procedure texts for inconsistencies across documents.

risks: Generic controls that do not fit a logistics company with flex workers
Procedures on paper that do not match AFAS settings
Over-control adds workload to the bookkeepers
research_questions: How many procedures exist, and how inconsistent are they today?
Can AFAS workflow settings be exported to compare against the approval matrix?
Did the last management letter points get fixed, and how long did drafting take?

tasks.short: Prepare the year-end figures and tax files so the external accountant can file VPB and other returns.

today.trigger: Year-end close and the external tax adviser's information request; monthly or quarterly VAT returns.
steps: Run trial balance and reconcile accounts in AFAS
Build the fiscal-to-commercial reconciliation and specifications in Excel
Collect supporting documents (fixed assets, provisions, non-deductible costs)
Send the package to the tax adviser and answer questions
drudgery: Rebuilding specifications that look much the same each year
Splitting costs into deductible and partly deductible (e.g. representation, company cars)
today.time_sinks: Specifications and the fiscal adjustments list, and rounds of questions from the adviser.

lenses.faster: Specifications and the fiscal adjustment list are generated from AFAS with last year's mapping, and AI pre-classifies cost lines that may be partly deductible.
lenses.autonomous: Throughout the year, transactions on sensitive accounts are tagged for tax treatment at booking, so year-end needs only review.
lenses.ambitious: A tax file that is ready within days of close, with every fiscal adjustment traceable, so the adviser bills fewer hours.
lenses.joy: No more hunting through ledger lines for lunches and gifts; the controller reviews the classification.
lenses.options: Show the effect of alternative treatments (e.g. provisions, investment deductions like KIA) on taxable profit before deciding with the adviser.
lenses.altitude: The controller maintains the tax mapping and classification rules and checks the output with the adviser.

tasks.human_edge: Signing off on positions, judging grey areas with the tax adviser, and carrying responsibility toward the Belastingdienst.
tasks.pattern_why: Mapping from ledger to fiscal specifications follows written rules on structured AFAS data; an LLM step only helps classify free-text cost descriptions.

steps: Scripted extract of trial balance and sensitive accounts from AFAS
Apply mapping rules to build specifications and fiscal adjustments
LLM step classifies unclear cost descriptions for deductibility with a confidence score
Controller reviews flagged lines and sends the package to the adviser
in_practice.human_gate: Controller and the external tax adviser approve the package and any return before filing.
data_needed: Last year's tax file and adviser comments
in_practice.logs_to: Tax file folder on SharePoint with mapping version and review notes

evidence.claim: Rule-based mapping from trial balance to tax specifications can be scripted.
LLMs classify free-text expense descriptions into tax categories with reviewable accuracy.

risks: Misclassification leads to a wrong return and penalties
Tax rules change yearly and mapping goes stale
Adviser's own process may not fit the new package
research_questions: How many adviser hours and controller hours does the current year-end tax file take?
How much of last year's specification could be reused unchanged?
Will the tax adviser accept a standard package format?

tasks.short: Work with the tax adviser on choices that lower tax: investments, timing, entity structure, VAT.

today.trigger: Budget season, large investment plans (trucks, warehouse equipment, solar panels), or adviser's annual meeting.
steps: List planned investments and expected results
Check possible schemes (KIA, EIA, MIA/Vamil) and timing effects
Discuss scenarios with the tax adviser
Propose choices to the Finance Director
drudgery: Checking scheme conditions and thresholds every year
today.time_sinks: Researching current scheme conditions and building scenario models.

lenses.faster: AI summarises current scheme conditions from official sources and fills a standing scenario model from the investment plan.
lenses.autonomous: When an investment request above a threshold enters the approval flow, a check runs for possible tax schemes and deadlines (such as notification periods for EIA/MIA).
lenses.ambitious: Every qualifying investment is checked for schemes in time, instead of only the big ones the adviser notices.
lenses.joy: Less reading of scheme texts; more time discussing real choices with the Finance Director.
lenses.options: Several scenarios for timing, lease versus buy and scheme use, side by side with the tax and cash effect.
lenses.altitude: The controller runs the tax planning model and scheme checklist and challenges the adviser with prepared scenarios.
reach: FP&A Analyst: tax lines in the forecast
Finance Director: first draft of investment business cases

tasks.human_edge: Weighing tax effects against business and reputational risk, and the relationship with the adviser and the Belastingdienst.
tasks.pattern_why: Scenarios and research can be generated, but choices carry liability and need expert judgement with the adviser.

in_practice.trigger: Investment request above threshold or annual budget round.
steps: Pull investment plan and forecast results
LLM summarises applicable schemes with source links for the adviser to verify
Scenario model computes tax and cash effects
Controller discusses with adviser and proposes to the Finance Director
in_practice.human_gate: Tax adviser checks scheme applicability; Finance Director decides.
data_needed: Current scheme conditions from RVO and Belastingdienst

evidence.claim: LLMs can summarise Dutch tax scheme conditions, but may be out of date or wrong without checking sources.

risks: Outdated or invented scheme conditions
Missed notification deadlines if the check is trusted blindly
Aggressive planning that clashes with company values
research_questions: How many schemes were missed or claimed late in the last three years?
How much of the adviser's fee is research the controller could prepare?
Can investment requests be routed through a check at approval time?

tasks.short: Set depreciation terms for trucks, racking and IT, and advise on buy, lease or dispose.

today.trigger: A new asset is capitalised, a lease ends, or management asks whether to buy or lease trucks or forklifts.
steps: Check asset category and useful life policy
Set up the asset and depreciation in AFAS
For decisions, build buy-versus-lease and disposal calculations in Excel
Advise the Finance Director and operations
drudgery: Entering asset cards one by one
today.time_sinks: Asset setup from invoices and one-off decision models.

lenses.faster: Capitalisation proposals with category and useful life are generated from the purchase invoice; a standard buy-lease-dispose model is filled from quotes.
lenses.autonomous: When an invoice on an investment account is posted, an asset card proposal is created in AFAS; leases near end of term trigger a renewal analysis.
lenses.ambitious: Fleet and equipment decisions across all three sites based on real lifetime cost, maintenance and residual values, not one request at a time.
lenses.joy: No typing of asset cards; the controller works on fleet decisions with operations.
lenses.options: For each truck or forklift decision: buy, operational lease, extend, or dispose, with cost, cash and IFRS 16 or Dutch GAAP effect shown.
lenses.altitude: The controller owns the asset policy and the decision model, and reviews proposals.

tasks.human_edge: Judging real useful life with the fleet manager, negotiating with lessors, and defending choices to the auditor.
tasks.pattern_why: Depreciation follows written policy on structured data and the decision model is arithmetic; an LLM only helps read invoices and quotes.

in_practice.trigger: Invoice posted on an investment account, or lease end within six months.
steps: Read invoice or quote and map to asset category
Apply useful life and residual value policy
Create asset card proposal in AFAS
For decisions, run the buy-lease-dispose model and draft advice
Controller approves card and advice
in_practice.human_gate: Controller approves each asset card and each advice before it goes to management.
data_needed: Maintenance costs and residual value data
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS fixed asset register and decision memos on SharePoint

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit includes a fixed asset module that calculates depreciation schedules.
Buy-versus-lease models are standard spreadsheet calculations that can be templated.

risks: Wrong category leads to wrong depreciation and audit adjustment
Residual value assumptions are poor for trucks
Lease accounting differs between reporting frameworks
research_questions: How many assets are capitalised per year and how long does setup take?
Is maintenance cost per truck and forklift available by asset?
Which reporting framework (Dutch GAAP or IFRS) applies to leases here?

role.altitude: From preparing analyses, evidence and procedures by hand to owning the finance control system: the data model, control rules, tax and asset mappings, and the assistant that answers budget holders, while reviewing exceptions and making the judgement calls.
reach: FP&A Analyst: variance commentary and capex forecast
Accountant: year-end specifications and fixed asset register
Bookkeeper: coding questions and VAT preparation
Finance Director: first drafts of MT finance pack and investment cases
Credit and Collections Officer: credit limit procedure drafts
role.ceiling_note: Roughly 40 percent of time on these tasks can be freed; the limits are data quality from AFAS and the agency portals, the auditor's and tax adviser's acceptance of AI-prepared material, and the controller's personal accountability for sign-off, tax positions and audit negotiations.
skills_to_grow: Designing data models and variance rules in Power BI
Writing and testing control rules for full-population checks
Reviewing AI output critically and keeping an audit trail
Prompting and grounding assistants on SharePoint policies
Coaching budget holders on their numbers
role.ambitious_version: A controller who runs continuous controls and cost-to-serve per customer and site, closes the month faster with a forecast the business trusts, and spends most time with site managers on margin decisions instead of on exports and evidence gathering.
